The book lists one exam topic for this chapter:
5.5 Describe remote access and site-to-site VPNs
(under 5.0 Security Fundamentals). Its Exam Essentials add two goals. The objectives below come from those two goals and the chapter text.
After this chapter you should be able to:
1. Explain what a VPN is and how it differs from a WAN link and a VLAN.
2. Name the VPN categories: remote access, site-to-site, extranet, and the provider-managed Layer 2 and Layer 3 MPLS VPNs.
3. Explain what IPsec is, what AH and ESP do, and the difference between transport mode and tunnel mode.
4. Explain why GRE has no security and why GRE over IPsec is used.
5. Configure and verify a GRE tunnel, and recognise the recursive routing error.

Which statement best describes a VPN?
A. A leased private line from a provider
B. A private network created across a public network, using tunnelling and usually encryption
C. A VLAN across two switches
D. A wireless network for guests
B - a VPN makes private connectivity over a public network such as the Internet.
A host in a remote office must appear local to a secure server VLAN. Which is the right tool?
B - VLANs are for physically local networks. A VPN extends the local view across a WAN.
Which two are enterprise-managed VPN categories?
A and C - MPLS VPNs and VPWS are provider-managed services.
Which VPN type gives partners and suppliers limited access for B2B traffic?
Extranet VPN - extranet VPNs are limited in what they let partners reach.
In a Layer 3 MPLS VPN, which router belongs to the customer?
A - CE is the customer edge. PE and P belong to the provider.
Which provider technology gives a multipoint, LAN-like Ethernet service?
B - VPLS makes sites share one virtual Ethernet broadcast domain. VPWS is point to point.
A remote user has no VPN software installed and uses only a web browser. What kind of VPN is this?
A clientless (browser-based) SSL/TLS VPN - no client install is needed. The book calls it a Web VPN.
What IP protocol number does ESP use?
B - IANA registry. 47 is GRE, 51 is AH, 115 is L2TP.
What IP protocol number does AH use?
51 - IANA registry. It is an IP protocol number, not a port.
Which UDP port is used by IKE, and which by NAT-T?
500 for IKE and 4500 for NAT-T - secondary sources.
Which IPsec protocol can provide encryption?
B - AH authenticates only. ESP can encrypt.
Which IPsec protocol authenticates as much of the IP header as possible?
AH - RFC 4302. ESP does not cover the outer IP header.
What does IPsec tunnel mode do to the original packet?
It wraps the whole packet and adds a new outer IP header - tunnel mode is typical between gateways.
In transport mode with ESP, what stays visible?
The original IP header - ESP encrypts the payload only in transport mode.
Which statement about plain IPsec (no GRE) is true according to the book?
A. It carries IP multicast and routing protocols easily
B. It cannot carry IP broadcast, multicast or non-IP traffic
C. It carries non-IP traffic natively
B - that is why GRE is added to carry routing protocols.
Which of these is asymmetric encryption?
C - RSA uses a key pair. The others are symmetric.
Which algorithms and groups does Cisco no longer recommend for IPsec?
DES, 3DES, MD5, and DH groups 1, 2 and 5 - use AES, SHA-2 and DH group 14 or higher. Cisco IOS XE IPsec guide.
What is the IP protocol number of GRE?
How many bytes of overhead does a basic GRE tunnel add, and where do they come from?
24 bytes: 20 for the outer IP header and 4 for the GRE header - checked by arithmetic.
On a 1500-byte Ethernet path, what are the GRE tunnel IP MTU and the TCP MSS?
IP MTU 1476 and TCP MSS 1436 - 1500 minus 24, and 1476 minus 40. Script-checked.
Does GRE encrypt the traffic it carries?
No - GRE offers no security. Add IPsec for encryption.
Which command creates a GRE tunnel interface numbered 5?
R-A has tunnel source 192.0.2.1 and destination 192.0.2.2. What must R-B use?
Source 192.0.2.2 and destination 192.0.2.1 - source and destination are mirror images.
Tunnel0 is up/up and the tunnel IPs ping, but PC-to-PC across the tunnel fails. What is the most likely cause?
No routes for the remote LANs point into the tunnel - the tunnel is a path. Routes decide what uses it.
What causes %TUN-5-RECURDOWN, and how do you fix it?
The router reaches the tunnel destination through the tunnel. Make the physical path the best route to the destination. - Cisco support document 22327.
Which technology uses one tunnel interface and one IPsec profile on the hub for all spokes, with dynamic spoke-to-spoke tunnels?
B - DMVPN is built from mGRE, NHRP and IPsec.
Which v2.0 exam objective covers IPsec VPNs?
4.5 - "Describe IPsec remote access and site-to-site VPNs (protocols and transport modes)". Official v2.0 outline.
A private network over a public one. Makes a remote host or site look local, with protection. Use a VLAN for local networks, a VPN for remote ones.
Remote access (user to site), site-to-site, extranet (limited partner access). Provider-managed: Layer 2 MPLS (VPWS, VPLS) and Layer 3 MPLS (CE, PE, P).
4.5 Describe IPsec remote access and site-to-site VPNs (protocols and transport modes). v1.1 is 5.5.
A framework at Layer 3. Protects IP only. Does not carry non-IP or multicast by itself.
, covers as much of the IP header as possible. ESP (protocol 50): encryption plus integrity, authentication, anti-replay; does not cover the outer header.
Transport: header inserted, original IP header kept (hosts). Tunnel: whole packet wrapped in a new IP header (gateways, site-to-site).
Negotiates keys and settings. UDP 500, and UDP 4500 with NAT-T.
Symmetric (AES, DES, 3DES) encrypts data fast. Asymmetric (RSA) uses a key pair. Avoid DES, 3DES, MD5, DH 1/2/5. Use AES, SHA-2, DH 14 or higher.
IP protocol 47. Carries any Layer 3 protocol. Stateless.
At least 24 bytes overhead (20 + 4). Open standard (RFC 2784).
GRE carries routing and multicast, IPsec encrypts it. DMVPN scales hub-and-spoke. VTI is IPsec without GRE overhead.
